flagship.headline: The Beatles' White Album reaches No. 1 on the Billboard 200
flagship.summary_line_1: The Beatles' double album The Beatles, known as the White Album, moved from No. 2 to No. 1 on the Billboard 200 dated December 28, 1968, its first week on top after entering the chart at No. 11 on December 14.
flagship.summary_line_2: The two-LP set had been released in November, and the clip below is Back in the U.S.S.R., the album's opening track, from the band's Topic channel.

events.headline: The Beatles' White Album reaches No. 1 on the Billboard 200
events.summary_line_1: The Beatles' double album The Beatles, known as the White Album, moved from No. 2 to No. 1 on the Billboard 200 dated December 28, 1968, its first week on top after entering the chart at No. 11 on December 14.
events.summary_line_2: The two-LP set had been released in November, and the clip below is Back in the U.S.S.R., the album's opening track, from the band's Topic channel.

events.headline: Marvin Gaye spends a third week at No. 1 with I Heard It Through the Grapevine
events.summary_line_1: Marvin Gaye's I Heard It Through the Grapevine held at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 dated December 28, 1968, its third week on top, with Stevie Wonder's For Once in My Life at No. 2 and Love Child by Diana Ross & the Supremes at No. 3.
events.summary_line_2: It had entered the Hot 100 at No. 34 on November 23, and the clip below is the single from Gaye's official Vevo channel.

events.headline: Stevie Wonder reaches his peak with For Once in My Life
events.summary_line_1: Stevie Wonder's For Once in My Life rose from No. 3 to its No. 2 peak on the Billboard Hot 100 dated December 28, 1968, held out of the top spot by Marvin Gaye's Grapevine.
events.summary_line_2: The Motown single had entered the chart at No. 79 on November 2, and the clip below is the song from Wonder's Topic channel.

events.headline: Classics IV reach their peak with Stormy
events.summary_line_1: Classics IV Featuring Dennis Yost's Stormy rose from No. 6 to its No. 5 peak on the Billboard Hot 100 dated December 28, 1968.
events.summary_line_2: The single had entered the chart at No. 80 on October 26, and the clip below is the song from the group's Topic channel.

events.headline: The Doors debut on the Hot 100 with Touch Me
events.summary_line_1: The Doors' Touch Me entered the Billboard Hot 100 dated December 28, 1968 at No. 72.
events.summary_line_2: The single came ahead of the band's 1969 album The Soft Parade, and the clip below is the single mix from the band's own channel.

events.headline: Johnny Cash debuts on the Hot 100 with Daddy Sang Bass
events.summary_line_1: Johnny Cash's Daddy Sang Bass entered the Billboard Hot 100 dated December 28, 1968 at No. 64.
events.summary_line_2: Cash's best-known crossover single was still Ring of Fire, and the clip below is Daddy Sang Bass from his official Vevo channel.

events.headline: The 4 Seasons debut on the Hot 100 with Electric Stories
events.summary_line_1: The 4 Seasons Featuring the "Sound of Frankie Valli" entered the Billboard Hot 100 dated December 28, 1968 with Electric Stories at No. 83.
events.summary_line_2: The group had topped the Hot 100 earlier in the decade with Walk Like a Man, and the clip below is Electric Stories from Frankie Valli's Topic channel.

events.headline: The Beach Boys reach their peak with Bluebirds Over the Mountain
events.summary_line_1: The Beach Boys' Bluebirds Over the Mountain rose from No. 67 to its No. 61 peak on the Billboard Hot 100 dated December 28, 1968.
events.summary_line_2: The single, a cover of Ersel Hickey's 1958 song, had entered the chart at No. 74 on December 14, and the clip below is the mono single mix from the band's Topic channel.

events.headline: The Miami Pop Festival opens at Gulfstream Park
events.summary_line_1: The Miami Pop Festival opened at Gulfstream Park in Hallandale, Florida, on December 28, 1968, the first of three days that ran through December 30, per setlist.fm.
events.summary_line_2: About 100,000 fans came over the weekend to two stages for what became known as the first major rock festival on the US East Coast, and the clip below is Both Sides Now by Joni Mitchell, one of the performers on the bill.

events.headline: The Beatles play the third night of Another Beatles Christmas Show at Hammersmith
events.summary_line_1: The Beatles played two shows at the Hammersmith Odeon in London on December 28, 1964, the third night of the run, alongside Freddie and the Dreamers, Sounds Incorporated and the Yardbirds, with Jimmy Savile as compère, per the Beatles Bible.
events.summary_line_2: Their 11-song closing set included I Feel Fine, and the clip below is that song from the band's official Vevo channel.

events.headline: The Beatles play the fourth night of their Christmas Show in Finsbury Park
events.summary_line_1: The Beatles played two more shows of The Beatles' Christmas Show at the Astoria Cinema in Finsbury Park, London, on December 28, 1963, closing a bill that included Cilla Black and Billy J. Kramer and the Dakotas, per the Beatles Bible.
events.summary_line_2: Their 25-minute, nine-song set opened with Roll Over Beethoven, and the clip below is that song from the band's Topic channel.

events.headline: Lenny Welch reaches his peak with Since I Fell for You
events.summary_line_1: Lenny Welch's Since I Fell for You rose from No. 5 to its No. 4 peak on the Billboard Hot 100 dated December 28, 1963.
events.summary_line_2: The single, a cover of Buddy Johnson's 1945 song, had entered the chart at No. 99 on October 26, and the clip below is Welch's recording from his Topic channel.

events.headline: Marvin Gaye reaches his peak with Can I Get a Witness
events.summary_line_1: Marvin Gaye's Can I Get a Witness rose from No. 26 to its No. 22 peak on the Billboard Hot 100 dated December 28, 1963.
events.summary_line_2: It had entered the chart at No. 97 on October 19, five years before Gaye's Grapevine topped the Hot 100, and the clip below is the song from his Topic channel.

events.headline: Rick Nelson debuts on the Hot 100 with For You
events.summary_line_1: Rick Nelson's For You entered the Billboard Hot 100 dated December 28, 1963 at No. 61.
events.summary_line_2: Nelson's Poor Little Fool had topped the chart in 1958, and the clip below is For You from his Topic channel.

events.headline: Lesley Gore debuts on the Hot 100 with You Don't Own Me
events.summary_line_1: Lesley Gore's You Don't Own Me entered the Billboard Hot 100 dated December 28, 1963 at No. 72.
events.summary_line_2: The song would climb to No. 2 on the chart in early 1964, and the clip below is the single from her official Vevo channel.

events.headline: The Beatles play the tenth night of their last Star-Club residency
events.summary_line_1: The Beatles played the Star-Club in Hamburg on December 28, 1962, the tenth date of their third and final residency there, per the Beatles Bible.
events.summary_line_2: Their next single, Please Please Me, came out in the UK on January 11, 1963, and the clip below is that song from the band's official catalog.
